Subject: Post-call follow-up: Sierra Analytics — throughput & latency SLOs / deployment next steps

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for your time this morning — good conversation and really helpful to see the production shaping up. This note captures the key pain points, the goals you called out, and proposed next steps so we have alignment before Neha digs into a topology proposal.

Summary of pain points (what you told us):
- Real-time routing engine must respond sub-60ms p95 for short completion requests (<=64 tokens) to avoid user-experience regressions.
- Batch scoring (offline/ETL) needs sustained throughput: ~15k embeddings/hour and ~2M short generations/day.
- Sensitive PII in traces requires VPC/private deployment and strict KMS integration.
- Current in-house infra approaches 6–8 GPU saturation under peak; you need predictable scaling + fallback.

Goals / success criteria:
1) Achieve p95 generation latency <= 60ms for 64-token inference across top 3 routes (routing, rerank, short-completion).
2) Sustained batch throughput for embeddings and async jobs with cost target ~30–40% less than current spend.
3) Private deployment (VPC + customer KMS) with audit logs available for SOC-type evidence.

Immediate asks we agreed on:
- Neha will propose two topology options by EOD Wednesday: Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) vs Private (VPC) with sizing and expected latency/throughput numbers.
- You will share your current network diagram and an average/peak QPS breakdown for the routing workload.
- We will provide a draft SLA language and an initial cost estimate for the two options.

Attachments included: sierra-proj-draft-map.pdf (mine), redwood-sla-template.docx (baseline wording).

Next steps / timeline:
- By 2026-12-08 18:00 PST: Neha sends topology + perf estimates + risk notes.
- By 2026-12-10: Joint tech session to walk the proposal with your infra team (30–45 min).

If the above matches your notes, please reply with any corrections and attach the network diagram you mentioned. Happy to loop in a dedicated account engineer if you prefer a deeper ops-to-ops session.

Best,

Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — that write-up looks right. A couple clarifications and additions from our side:

Corrections / clarifications:
- The 60ms p95 target is correct for the top-level routing call (our UX bucket). For rerank and multi-pass scoring we can accept p95 <= 120ms, but p99 should remain reasonable.
- Peak routing QPS today: 750 requests/s (30% of traffic concentrated in a 10-minute burst window). Average QPS: ~220.
- Batch embedding jobs are currently run nightly; 15k/hr was a conservative estimate — our true goal is 25k/hr during heavy ETL windows.

We've attached the current network + infra diagram (sierra-network-diagram.v1.pdf). A couple of notes on constraints:
- All outbound traffic must originate from our VPC NAT; jump hosts currently sit behind a strict firewall.
- KMS is AWS KMS with strict key rotation policy; we will need Redwood to integrate with our KMS and provide audit/event logs.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll flag the 12/10 joint session and include our lead infra engineer Priya Shah.
- Please have Neha include expected cold-start behavior for model variants (we saw variability today).

Appreciate the clear timeline.

—Alex Torres

Alex / Priya — hi, Neha from Redwood engineering. Following Monica’s summary and your notes I sketched two concrete topology options with estimated latency and throughput expectations. Attaching a quick topology sketch (rdw-topology-proposal-20261208.png). Below are the highlights and trade-offs — I tried to be explicit about assumptions so we can iterate quickly.

Option A — Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) in Redwood Dedicated (recommended if cost predictability is priority):
- Topology: Dedicated GPU nodes (8x A100-equivalent) behind a lightweight routing layer in Redwood Dedicated, private peering to your VPC via NAT/Transit gateway. No model weights stored in your VPC; data-in-motion encrypted and KMS for key management.
- Expected latency: p95 ~ 45–55ms for 64-token short completions (single-token streaming offload), p99 ~ 80–95ms. Assumes single-turn requests, SIMD-optimized kernels, and async KV cache hit rate >= 70%.
- Throughput: Sustained per-cluster throughput ~900–1,200 requests/s (concurrent small requests) with autoscaling buffer for 10–15% bursts. Batch job throughput easily meets 25k embeddings/hr when scheduled across off-peak windows.
- Cold-start: warm pool maintained; cold-start tail < 150ms for scale-ups if autoscaling adds nodes.
- Pros: predictable performance, simpler fallback, SLAs available.
- Cons: higher fixed monthly commit.

Option B — Private deployment (full VPC & weights in-customer subnet) — recommended if data residency/KMS-in-customer is required:
- Topology: Customer-hosted model storage with Redwood private control plane; inference runtime deployed in your VPC (node sizing: 6x H100-equivalent for initial), direct access to KMS, audit logs shipped to your SIEM.
- Expected latency: p95 ~ 50–70ms for 64-token short completions depending on inter-node network and NAT egress constraints; p99 ~ 90–120ms.
- Throughput: Designed for sustained throughput at 1,000 requests/s with burst handling using local autoscaling. Batch throughput target 25k/hr met with parallelized embedding workers.
- Cold-start: slightly higher variability (tail up to 220ms) if VMs scale from zero. We recommend a small warm cushion to mitigate.
- Pros: full control of keys/weights, straightforward compliance.
- Cons: higher ops ownership for Sierra, network constraints can impact p95.

Model & config notes (common to both):
- Suggested model family: Redwood-verified OPTX-13B quantized to 4-bit (Q4) for middle ground. For the routing low-latency tight p95, consider a trimmed LLM baseline (OPTX-7B) with context-limited prompt templates to reduce per-token work.
- KV cache: enable customer-specific prefix caching; we estimate 65–75% prefix reuse on the routing workload which materially reduces p95.
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch size 32, target latency budget 30–40ms (so batching window < 6ms).
- Fallbacks: canonical plan — primary dedicated cluster + fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant with graceful reroute to reduce outages during scale events.

Assumptions called out:
- 64-token request size used for p95 estimates. If typical requests trend >128 tokens, numbers will change.
- Network RTT from your VPC to Redwood edge assumed <8ms; if higher, add ~8–15ms to p95.

Risk notes:
- If NAT/firewall rules restrict persistent peering, keep a short maintenance window to test.
- KMS integration will require a short onboarding (1–2 weeks) with your security team for key policies and audit export setup.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm which topology you prefer (A or B) and whether a canary run (2-week) is OK.
- If A: we’ll produce a sizing + commit recommendation and a cost delta.
- If B: we’ll produce an infra runbook, required IAM/KMS changes, and an ops handoff checklist.
- Schedule: We can present a 30–45m tech walkthrough on 2026-12-10 — Monica, can you confirm time windows?

Attachment: rdw-topology-proposal-20261208.png (single-page sketch).

Happy to jump on a quick call with Priya and your infra folks to walk through the pieces.
